questions.question: Which type of X-ray emission is typically analyzed in EPMA for determining the composition of alloys?
In the context of EPMA, what is the purpose of performing a 'ZAF correction' when analyzing alloys?

answers.a: To correct for surface roughness of the alloy
answers.b: To account for differences in atomic number, absorption, and fluorescence between the sample and standards
answers.c: To enhance the resolution of the X-ray detectors
answers.d: To increase the X-ray emission from the alloy

questions.question: In the analysis of a nickel-based superalloy using EPMA, the analyst observes anomalously high concentrations of a light element. Which factors could be responsible for this observation, and how should they be mitigated?

answers.a: Contamination from the vacuum chamber; mitigate by thorough cleaning
answers.b: Beam-induced sample damage; mitigate by reducing the beam current
answers.c: X-ray fluorescence from neighboring elements; mitigate by using appropriate standards and applying corrections
answers.d: High electron dose; mitigate by using a lower accelerating voltage

questions.question: What role does the accelerating voltage play in determining the depth of analysis during EPMA of an alloy, and how does this influence the measured composition?

answers.a: Higher accelerating voltage increases the analysis depth, potentially incorporating signals from underlying phases and affecting the measured composition
answers.b: Higher accelerating voltage reduces the analysis depth, leading to more surface-sensitive measurements
answers.c: Accelerating voltage has no impact on the depth of analysis
answers.d: Higher accelerating voltage decreases X-ray intensity, complicating compositional analysis

questions.question: In EPMA analysis of a multi-phase alloy, how can the presence of elements with very different atomic numbers in adjacent phases complicate the quantitative analysis, and what strategies can be employed to address this?

answers.a: It can lead to underestimation of light elements; employ peak deconvolution and proper ZAF corrections to address this
answers.b: It results in beam scattering; reduce beam current and use low atomic number standards
answers.c: It enhances X-ray production; use a lower accelerating voltage to minimize this effect
answers.d: It complicates the focusing of the electron beam; use high-precision focusing techniques
